$comment: PLACEHOLDER RECORDS — the EOD report, answering 'what did they actually get done'. Stands in for GET /api/v1/admin/team/reports?date= and GET/PUT/POST /api/v1/admin/team/reports/{date}, plus POST /api/v1/admin/team/reports/{id}/acknowledge. ONE per member per business day, unique on (memberId, businessDate). The completed list is PRE-FILLED from that morning's plan and from anything completed that day, and ticking a line COMPLETES the work item — so 'what they said they would do' and 'what they did' are a diff, not two paragraphs somebody has to compare. THE HOURS ARE NOT IN THIS PAYLOAD and must never be: they are read from the attendance row. A report that lets a person type their own hours is not a record of anything. `acknowledgedBy` is the senior's read receipt — it exists so a member can see that the thing they wrote was read.
$comment_today: There are NO reports for 2026-08-28. It is 14:20 and the day is not over — an EOD report missing at 14:20 is not missing, it is early. The Reports screen must not count it as outstanding until the business day has ended, which is why 'not submitted' is derived against the clock rather than against the mere absence of a row.

$comment_missing: Members 70 and 86 filed nothing for 2026-08-27. Member 70 also left his attendance row open that night — the same person, the same evening, and the two facts are recorded independently rather than one being inferred from the other. That is deliberate: a missing EOD does not prove somebody stopped working, and an unclosed day does not prove they did. The screen shows both and lets a person draw the conclusion.
